AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 19, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8056-016-139; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: Knights of Columbus; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk City Employees Association.

  III.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager; regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

  IV.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  54957(b)(1): City Manager.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Pastor George Bojorquez
  New Creation Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Isabella Alvarez, 5th grade
  William Orr School

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  City Council to proclaim April 29, 2022 as Arbor Day in the City of Norwalk.

  City Council to proclaim the month of April as Public Schools Month in the City of Norwalk.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.
   2.  Caren Spilsbury, Norwalk Chamber of Commerce Quarterly Update.

  3.  Commander Salvador Becerra, Norwalk Sheriff Station Quarterly Update.

  4.  Department Highlights video – Norwalk Transportation Department.

  5.  Egg-Stravagant Egg Hunt video.

  6.  Santa Fe Springs High School Raising Awareness for upcoming Prom Drinking & Driving spotlight
  video.

  7.  Week in Review video.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of March
  31 and April 5, 2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period March 6, 2022 – March
  19, 2022 totaling $944,995.50 and March 20, 2022 – April 2, 2022 totaling $942,746.86. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  March 29 – April 11, 2022 in the total amount of $1,651,366.53. 640

  Warrant Register

  5.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Alicia
  Washington. 830-23

  Report

  6.  ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS - Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.

  b.  Both of the following circumstances exist (i) The state of emergency continues to directly impact
  the ability of the members to meet safely in person and (ii) City Council continues to impose or
  recommend measures to promote social distancing including remote or hybrid meeting
  participation. 825

  Report

  7.  REQUEST FOR USE OF CIVIC CENTER LAWN FOR NORWALK FARMERS MARKET - Staff
  recommends City Council approve the Norwalk Farmers Market on a weekly basis every Tuesday and
  Saturday through the end of the 2022 calendar year and waive the security deposit as requested
  consistent with past practice. 920-01-02

  Report

  8.  APPROVAL OF NORWALK SENIOR CITIZENS CENTER, INC. (NSCC, INC.) BOARD OF
  DIRECTORS - Staff recommends City Council approve the nominations of Yolanda Rodriguez,
  President; Marlene Hardy, Vice President; Ralph Hogg, Treasurer; Bobbie Wakefield, Secretary; and
  Guadalupe Leclercq, Member At Large to the Norwalk Senior Citizens Center, Inc. Board of Directors
   for one-year terms to expire December 31, 2022. 425-02-04

  Report

  9.  VOLKSWAGEN MITIGATION TRUST FUND TRANSIT BUS FUNDING AGREEMENTS - Staff
  recommends City Council authorize the City Manager to execute Volkswagen Mitigation Trust Fund
  Transit Bus Funding Agreements G-92163-A1 and G-92166-A1, in the amount of $180,000 per
  agreement, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 810-22/1105

  Report

  10. PROJECT ESTIMATE UPDATE FOR STUDEBAKER ROAD AT HALCORT AVENUE, PROJECT NO.
  7241 – PROJECT STATUS – Receive and file. 1005-04-7241

  Report

  11. RESOLUTION NO. 22-20 – AUTHORIZING SUBMITTAL OF APPLICATION(S) FOR CALRECYCLE
  GRANTS – Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-20, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING SUBMITTAL OF APPLICATION(S) FOR
  CALRECYCLE GRANTS. 1065-04-01

  Report

  12. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT – UTILITIES PROGRAM MANAGEMENT AND UTILITIES
  ENGINEERING SUPPORT SERVICES – RESOLUTION NO. 22-21 - BUDGET AMENDMENT – Staff
  recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-21, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE AVAILABLE ENTERPRISE FUNDS FOR PROFESSIONAL
  SERVICES FOR UTILITIES PROGRAM MANAGEMENT AND UTILITIES ENGINEERING
  SUPPORT IN FISCAL YEAR 2021/22, in the amount of $16,500; and,

  b.  approve the Amendment with Bucknam and Associates Inc. to extend the Agreement to provide
  such services for Fiscal Year 2022/23, and provide an increase of $82,500 to the maximum
  compensation to cover the extra funds needed for Fiscal Year 2021/22 and Utility Programs
  Management and Utilities Engineering Support Services for Fiscal Year 2022/23; and authorize the
  City Manager to execute the Amendment, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the
  City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 810-02/1070-05

  Report

  13. SECURITY SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM – PHASE 1 – RESOLUTION NO. 22-22 - BUDGET
  AMENDMENT - Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-22, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK AUTHORIZING AN AMENDMENT TO THE FISCAL YEAR 2021/22 ADOPTED
  BUDGET TO APPROPRIATE FUNDS FOR THE SECURITY SURVEILLANCE SYSTEM
  PROJECT, in the amount of $672,500; and

  b.  award a contract to Innova Global Technology Inc. for the purchase and installation of Verkada
  security surveillance cameras and system at six City facilities in the amount of $672,500; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments for Phase I, provided
  that sufficient funds are available in the adopted budget for the applicable fiscal year, on behalf of
  the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 950

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  14. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report
   15. NORWALK HOUSING AUTHORITY APPOINTMENT - Staff recommends City Council re-appoint
  Mayor Ramirez to a four-year term ending April 30, 2026. 315-05-01

  Report

ORDINANCES

  16. ORDINANCE NO. 22-1730 - AMENDING TITLE 10 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  INCORPORATE GUIDELINES FOR PARKING PERMITS - Staff recommends City Council introduce
  by title only Ordinance No. 22-1730, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AMENDING
  CHAPTERS 10.04, 10.08, 10.09, 10.10, AND 10.12 OF TITLE 10 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL
  CODE TO INCORPORATE ADMINISTRATIVE AND PROGRAM GUIDELINES PERTAINING TO
  PARKING PERMITS FROM THE ADOPTED PARKING ACTION PLAN, and schedule for second
  reading.

  Report

  17. ORDINANCE NO. 22-1731 – AMENDING CHAPTER 8.56 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE
  ADDING NEW AND AMENDING CURRENT STANDARDS FOR FORECLOSED AND ABANDONED
  PROPERTIES - Staff recommends City Council introduce Ordinance No. 22- 1731, AN ORDINANCE
  OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AMENDING CHAPTER 8.56 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  INCLUDE STANDARDS FOR BOARDING, FENCING, AND MAINTAINING VACANT PROPERTIES
  AND AMENDING STANDARDS FOR FORECLOSED AND ABANDONED PROPERTIES, and
  schedule for second reading. 860-02

  Report

REPORTS

  18. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – APRIL EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE – Receive and
  file. 710-07

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated April 14, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
